patients.label: 19-year-old male with congenital abnormalities and intellectual disability diagnosed with stage IV primary biliary cholangitis with autoimmune hepatitis features and a 14q24.1q24.2 deletion
attribution_limitations: The Table 1 day −7 liver panel values (AST 105, ALT 66, ALP 237, GGT 670, total bilirubin 1.1, direct bilirubin 0.5) equal the numbers in the case-report text, and the day 10 copper 159, manganese 2.6 and AMA-M2/other autoantibody negatives equal the workup text, but the text never names those days, so the source does not identify them as the same measurement; they are kept as separate facts. By contrast, the age-3 AST/ALP statement and the 4- and 6-month AMA-M2 statements name the same time points as Table 1 columns and are merged with those cells.

The discussion lists AMA positivity among the bases of the PBC diagnosis, but the AMA-M2 immunoblot during the workup was negative and AMA-M2 positivity is reported only 4 months after treatment began, i.e. after the diagnosis.

The abstract says the patient presented with abnormal liver enzymes and pruritus "for more than 5 years"; the case text dates pruritus onset to after age 13 and the AST/ALP increases to age 3. The two statements are compatible (not a conflict), but the abstract duration is imprecise and its scope over the enzyme abnormality is unclear.

The authors state the patient has not yet met the 2022 APASL diagnostic requirements for PBC with AIH features, yet describe the diagnosis as supported by interface hepatitis and treatment response; AIH features are kept provisional.
ALP reference intervals differ: the text gives normal <122 U/L while Table 1 lists age-banded ranges (16–19 yr 58–237; ≥19 yr 28–94). Both are kept as printed; no flags were derived from either.

Hedged exclusions (drug-induced liver injury "extremely low" likelihood, hepatocellular carcinoma "low possibility") are not explicit exclusions and are recorded as possible differentials; the cause of hepatocerebral degeneration is hedged and not recorded.
Footnote (c) says the diagnosis was made a week after discharge, while the biopsy is described before treatment without a date; the source does not date the biopsy relative to discharge.

evidence.quote: (A) Nodule formation with a thick fibrous septa was noted and considered representative of advanced cirrhosis (Masson's trichrome stain).
(B) No interlobular bile duct was noted in the enlarged portal tract.
(C) Immunohistochemical staining for CK7 revealed a complete absence of bile ducts in the portal tracts.
(D) The periportal hepatocytes showed marked ballooning changes with abundant copper deposition (arrows) (Rhodanine stain).

limitations: Table 1 cells marked NT (not tested) are not individual observations; 70 NT cells were not recorded as facts and appear only as missing cells in the measurement series.

Table 1 footnote says bold results are abnormal; bold marking exists in the raw XML but not in the quotable source text, so no flags were taken from it or from reference ranges; abnormality is recorded only where the text says so (age-3 AST/ALP via the merged text statement).

Text and Table 1 values that coincide numerically are merged only where the text names the same time point as the table column (age-3 AST/ALP, AMA-M2 at 4 and 6 months after treatment); the undated workup values are kept separate.

Discussion statements about other published pediatric PBC cases (Table 2) and general prognosis are not patient facts. Copper and manganese correlation with GGT is a patient-level analytic claim without values and was not recorded; the prognostic risk-factor statement (baseline cirrhosis, ductopenia, PBC with AIH features) and the hedged "long-term follow-up may be warranted" are discussion interpretation, not recorded as facts or care plans.
Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the single JPEG is inspected in the separate visual target.

claims.text: A 19-year-old male born late preterm at 36 + 5 weeks had multiple congenital abnormalities (left thumb polydactyly, webbed neck, facial dysmorphism, patent ductus arteriosus and a left ectopic kidney). He had surgical PDA ligation without complications, neurodevelopmental delay with intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, repeated childhood admissions for bronchopulmonary infection, mild AST and ALP increases from age 3, and pruritus after age 13.

claims.text: In 2022 he was brought in for elevated liver enzymes found at health checkups; he was anicteric with enlarged liver and spleen, and sonography suggested cirrhosis. Virology and autoimmune immunoblot serology were negative, IgG was slightly elevated, urinary and serum copper and serum manganese were increased, and MRCP, CT, endoscopy and brain MRI were performed. A liver biopsy showed advanced cirrhosis, ductopenia, copper deposition and interface hepatitis.

evidence.quote: The patient was brought to our hospital in 2022 because his liver enzyme levels were discovered to be elevated during health checkups.
Upon examination, he was found to be anicteric
Upon examination, he was found to be anicteric, and his spleen and liver were discovered to be enlarged on palpation.
Abdominal sonography was therefore arranged. The sonography report revealed hepatosplenomegaly with a coarse liver and globular changes in the liver indicative of liver cirrhosis.
The patient was referred to our gastrointestinal department for further examination.
Given the presence of an unidentified hepatitis with cholestasis complicated by liver cirrhosis, the patient was admitted to our ward for further evaluation.
Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) was performed to diagnose possible biliary tract disease.
The MRCP revealed masses occupying both lobes of the liver, indicating the presence of severe macronodular cirrhosis.
Triphasic liver computed tomography accompanied by a thorough study of tumor markers indicated a low possibility of hepatocellular carcinoma.
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed no esophageal varices.
Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed increased signal intensity on T1WI over the bilateral globus pallidus
AST level, 105 U/L (normal: ≤34 U/L)
alanine aminotransferase (ALT) level, 66 U/L (normal: ≤36 U/L)
gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase (GGT) level, 670 U/L (normal: <71 U/L)
ALP level, 237 U/L (normal: <122 U/L)
The results of virological tests, including those for hepatitis A–C viruses, Epstein–Barr virus, and cytomegalovirus, were negative.

Immunoblot analysis to detect autoimmune liver diseases revealed negative results for circulating autoantibodies, including AMA-M2, anti-soluble liver antigen/liver–pancreas antibodies, anti-liver cytosol type 1 antibodies, anti-liver-kidney microsome type 1 antibodies, anti-smooth muscle antibodies; antinuclear antibodies; and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies.
Immunoglobulin (IG) tests revealed slightly elevated IgG levels (1,840 mg/dl, normal: <1,600 mg/dl)

Tests to diagnose Wilson's disease (WD) revealed an increase in the patient's 24-h urinary copper levels, with levels of 57 µg/day and 1,290 µg/day being detected before and after the penicillamine challenge test, respectively (normal: ≤40 µg/day).
His serum copper level was also elevated (159 µg/dl, normal: <140 µg/dl).
The serum manganese level was therefore measured and was found to have slightly increased to 2.6 µg/L (normal: <2.4 µg/L).
Due to the lack of an accurate diagnosis, a liver biopsy was performed.
Pathological examination revealed advanced liver cirrhosis (Figure 1A) with a paucity of interlobular bile ducts
with a paucity of interlobular bile ducts; this finding was confirmed by the results of immunohistochemical (IHC) staining for CK7 (Figures 1B,C)
a marked increase in copper deposition in the periportal areas (Figure 1D)
Interface hepatitis was also noted.

claims.text: Stage IV primary biliary cholangitis with features of autoimmune hepatitis was diagnosed, Wilson disease was ruled out, and whole exome sequencing found no pathogenic variants for hereditary cholestatic disorders. Array comparative genomic hybridization showed a 3.89 Mb de novo 14q24.1q24.2 deletion.

evidence.quote: On the basis of these findings, the patient was considered to have stage IV PBC according to the Ludwig classiﬁcation.

PBC was diagnosed in accordance with the 2022 Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL) clinical practice guidance on the basis of the presence of elevated ALP and GGT levels, AMA positivity and typical hepatic histopathological features
These findings were suggestive of significant inflammatory activity and coexisting AIH.
the pathological findings of severe interface hepatitis, along with the patient's favorable response to treatment with ursodeoxycholic acid and steroids, support the diagnosis
WD could be ruled out as it is not associated with marked bile duct loss
whole exon sequencing was conducted, which did not identify any pathogenic variant loci associated with potential monogenic hereditary cholestatic liver disorders upon analysis

The results revealed a 3.89 Mb de novo deletions of 14q24.1q24.2, including 22 Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) genes: RAD51B, ZFP36L1, ACTN1, DCAF5, EXD2, GALNT16, ERH, SLC39A9, SUSD6, SRSF5, SLC10A1, SMOC1, SLC8A3, COX16, SYNJ2BP, ADAM21, ADAM20, MED6, TTC9, MAP3K9, PCNX1, and SIPA1L1.
The results revealed a 3.89 Mb de novo deletions of 14q24.1q24.2

claims.text: After the diagnosis he received ursodeoxycholic acid and prednisolone. Cholestasis and liver enzymes improved markedly after 1 month and remained improved one year after initial treatment, with lower serum copper and manganese and improved tremor, ataxia and pruritus. AMA-M2 was positive 4 months and negative 6 months after treatment.

evidence.quote: After the diagnosis was made, the patient was administered 13 mg/kg/day ursodeoxycholic acid and 0.5 mg/kg/day prednisolone.
Follow-up examinations revealed marked improvements in both cholestasis and liver enzyme levels after 1 month of treatment
these levels have been maintained to date (i.e., one year after the initial treatment)
A decrease in the serum copper and manganese levels was also observed (Table 1).
repeated testing of circulating autoantibodies revealed that the patient was positive for AMA-M2 4 months after the treatment

Text and Table 1 values that coincide numerically are merged only where the text names the same time point as the table column (age-3 AST/ALP, AMA-M2 at 4 and 6 months after treatment); the undated workup values are kept separate.

evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Histopathological examination of the liver biopsy specimen. (A) Nodule formation with a thick fibrous septa was noted and considered representative of advanced cirrhosis (Masson's trichrome stain). (B) No interlobular bile duct was noted in the enlarged portal tract. Interface inflammation was also noted (hematoxylin and eosin stain). (C) Immunohistochemical staining for CK7 revealed a complete absence of bile ducts in the portal tracts. (D) The periportal hepatocytes showed marked ballooning changes with abundant copper deposition (arrows) (Rhodanine stain).
